```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6,
                      fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 96, fig.align = "center")
```

Every plot is an ordinary ggplot, so `+ labs()`, `+ facet_wrap()`,
`+ theme()` and any other layer work. The default look is a
Nature/Science-style theme with a colour-vision-checked palette and journal
column widths.

```{r fit}
library(cleanresults)

d <- cr_example_data()
p <- d[!duplicated(d$id), ]       # one row per person, for raw-data plots

res <- clean_regress(
  d,
  dvs = c(trust = "linear", share = "logistic"),
  predictors = ~ condition * female,
  random = ~ (1 | id),
  contrasts = "condition",
  dv_labels = c(trust = "Trust", share = "Shared")
)
```

## Group means with significance brackets

From a fitted model, the means are estimated marginal means with the model's
own (robust) SEs, and the brackets use the same adjusted contrasts as the
table, so a star on the figure always matches the table and text.

```{r means}
cr_plot_means(res, "trust", "condition")
```

```{r means-by}
cr_plot_means(res, "trust", "condition", by = "female", type = "dot", p = "value")
```

From a data frame you get raw means with SE, SD, or CI and Welch *t*-test
brackets (Holm-adjusted by default):

```{r means-raw}
cr_plot_means(p, "trust", "condition", type = "raincloud")
```

Brackets: `comparisons = "ref"` (versus the first level), `"all"`, `"sig"`, or
named pairs; `p = "stars"`, `"value"`, or `"none"`. *P*-values always come
from the full set of pairs, so showing fewer brackets never changes them.

## Interactions

```{r interaction}
cr_plot_interaction(res, "trust", "condition", "female")
```

With a continuous variable on the x axis you get predicted lines and ribbons:

```{r interaction-continuous}
res_age <- clean_regress(d, dvs = c(trust = "linear"),
                         predictors = ~ condition * age)
cr_plot_interaction(res_age, "trust", "age", "condition")
```

## Coefficients and distributions

The forest plot has a thick 90% interval inside the thin 95% interval, and a
dashed line at no effect.

```{r coef}
cr_plot_coef(res)
```

```{r hist}
cr_plot_hist(p, "age", by = "condition")
```

## Captions, themes, colours, export

Every plot carries a method note for the caption:

```{r note}
g <- cr_plot_means(res, "trust", "condition") + ggplot2::labs(title = "Study 1")
attr(g, "cr_note")
```

- **Themes:** `theme_cr("nature")` (default), `"psychsci"`, `"jcr"`,
  `"polsci"`. Pass `style =` to any plot, or add `theme_cr()` to your own.
- **Colours:** `cr_palette(n)` picks validated defaults (2 groups: teal,
  terracotta; 3: slate control, navy, terracotta; 4: navy, teal, terracotta,
  purple). Every pair in them stays distinguishable for colour-blind readers.
  Slate and teal are almost identical for red-blind readers, so avoid using
  them together. Other palettes: `"teal_terracotta"`, `"forest_lilac"`,
  `"nordic_ochre"`, `"partisan_bridge"`. Set one project-wide with
  `options(cleanresults.palette = "forest_lilac")`, or use `scale_fill_cr()`.
- **Export:** `.pdf` (vector, fonts embedded via cairo), `.svg`, `.eps`, and
  `.png`/`.tiff` at 600 dpi. `width` takes millimetres or `"1col"` (88 mm),
  `"1.5col"`, and `"2col"` (178 mm).

```{r export}
cr_save(g, file.path(tempdir(), "fig1.pdf"), width = "1col")
cr_palette(3)
```
